Heatmaps

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/heatmaps.Rmd
heatmaps.Rmd

Basic Heatmap 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_heatmap(z = volcano)

Categorical Axes 

m <- matrix(rnorm(9), nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
go_figure() |>
  add_heatmap(
    x = c("a", "b", "c"),
    y = c("d", "e", "f"),
    z = m
  )

Sequential Colorscales: Greys

The colorscale property accepts the name of a built-in colorscale (see named_colorscale()).

go_figure() |>
  add_heatmap(z = volcano, colorscale = "Greys")

Custom colorscales

colorscale also accepts a vector of colors, which are spaced evenly from 0 to 1.

go_figure() |>
  add_heatmap(z = volcano, colorscale = c("red", "green"))

Or, you can do the scaling yourself and give the colorscale as a two-column data frame of stops and colors…

vals <- unique(scales::rescale(c(volcano)))
o <- order(vals, decreasing = FALSE)
cols <- scales::col_numeric("Blues", domain = NULL)(vals)
colz <- setNames(data.frame(vals[o], cols[o]), NULL)
go_figure() |>
  add_heatmap(z = volcano, colorscale = colz)
